calls.title: Work Premises Accident
calls.about: A warehouse worker hurt on a loading dock at work. Listen for how the VA separates the workers' compensation side from a possible third-party claim, and gets the incident report and the employer's details.
listen_for: Workers' compensation vs. a third-party claim (the contractor)
The incident report and who it was given to
Treatment so far and who is paying
A firm commitment and a set callback time
lines: Thank you for calling Harbor and Pine Injury Law. This is Amy, intake specialist. How may I help you today?
Hi, yeah. My name is Marcus Bell. I got hurt at work last week and my buddy told me I should call a lawyer.
I'm sorry to hear that, Marcus. I'd like to ask you a few questions so the attorney can review what happened. This will take about ten minutes. Is now a good time?
Yeah, I'm home. I'm not working right now anyway.
Thank you. May I have your full name spelled out, and the best number to reach you?
Marcus, M A R C U S, Bell, B E L L. My cell is seven zero two, five five five, zero one four eight.
Seven zero two, five five five, zero one four eight. And your date of birth?
Thank you. What date did the accident happen, and where?
October twenty first. At the distribution warehouse on Cheyenne Avenue, where I work. I'm a forklift loader.
Can you walk me through what happened?

So there's a cleaning company that comes in at night. They mopped the loading dock and didn't put out any signs. I stepped off the forklift, my feet went out from under me, and I landed on my back and my right wrist.
Is the cleaning company part of your employer, or a separate business?
Separate. They're contractors. Bright Shine Commercial Cleaning, it's on their vests.
That's helpful, thank you. Did you report the accident to your supervisor?
Yes. My supervisor, Dana, filled out an incident report that same night. I didn't get a copy though.
That's fine. We can request it. Were there any witnesses, or cameras on the dock?
Two guys on my shift saw it. And there are cameras on every dock door.
Good. Now, your injuries. Did you get medical treatment?
They sent me to the company's urgent care. The wrist is fractured, it's in a cast, and my lower back has been killing me. They want me to do physical therapy.
Has a workers' compensation claim been opened for you?
I think so. I got a letter with a claim number from some insurance company. Is that the same as suing?

It's a separate process. I can't give legal advice, but the attorney will explain how a workers' compensation claim and a claim against another company, like the cleaning contractor, can work together. Please keep that letter and bring the claim number to your consultation.
Okay. Will I have to pay for this? I'm already missing work.

Our attorneys handle injury cases on a contingency fee basis. That means there's no fee up front, and the attorney is only paid if there's a recovery. The attorney will go over the exact terms with you.
Have you spoken to anyone from the cleaning company or their insurance?
If anyone does, you can politely take their name and number and let us know before you give a statement. Have you signed anything about the accident, other than the work forms?

Thank you, Marcus. Let me recap. You were injured on October twenty first on the loading dock at work, when you slipped on a floor mopped by Bright Shine Commercial Cleaning with no warning signs. You fractured your right wrist and hurt your lower back, you were treated at the company urgent care, and your supervisor Dana made an incident report. Is that correct?
Our attorney will review your case today. Can we schedule your consultation for tomorrow at ten in the morning, by phone at this number?

Perfect. You'll receive a text confirming the appointment and a link to our intake packet. Please have your workers' compensation letter, your urgent care paperwork, and the names of the two witnesses ready. Is there anything else I can help you with?
No, that's all. Thank you, Amy.
Thank you for calling Harbor and Pine, Marcus. Rest that wrist, and we'll talk tomorrow at ten.

calls.title: Demanding Slip and Fall Client
calls.about: A grocery-store slip and fall, with a caller who wants the attorney right now and a promise of money. Listen for how the VA stays calm, sets proper expectations, and still gets every detail.
listen_for: Staying calm with a demanding caller
No promises about money or outcome
Store incident report, photos and witnesses
Setting expectations about when the attorney calls back
lines: Thank you for calling Harbor and Pine Injury Law. This is Amy, intake specialist. How may I help you?
Yes, I need to talk to the lawyer. Not an assistant. The lawyer. Right now.

I understand you'd like to speak with the attorney. I'm the person who gathers your information first, so that when the attorney calls you, they already know your case and don't waste your time. May I have your name?
Linda Ramos. And I've already told this story three times today.
I'm sorry, Ms. Ramos. I'll make sure you only have to tell it once here. What's the best number to reach you?
Seven two five, five five five, zero three six two.
Seven two five, five five five, zero three six two. And your date of birth?
Thank you. When and where did you fall?

Saturday, November first, at the Valley Fresh Market on Rainbow Boulevard. There was a puddle by the frozen food aisle, no sign, nothing. I went down hard on my left hip. And I want to know how much I'm going to get, because I have bills.

I hear you, and I know the bills are stressful. I can't promise an amount, and no honest firm can on the first call. What I can do is get the attorney everything they need to evaluate your case quickly. Did you see what the liquid was?
It was clear, like water from the freezer case. It was leaking. An employee even said, oh, that's been leaking all morning.
Do you remember that employee's name, or what they looked like?
His tag said Kevin. Young guy, red apron.
Thank you, that's important. Did the store make an incident report?
The manager did, but they wouldn't give me a copy. And they offered me a fifty dollar gift card. Like that's going to cover anything.
Did you accept the gift card or sign anything?
That's good. Please don't sign anything from the store or their insurance. Did you take any photos?
My daughter took pictures of the puddle and the freezer, and of me on the floor.
Please keep those photos exactly as they are. Did you get medical treatment?
I went to the emergency room that night. They did X-rays, no break, but a bad bruise on the hip and they said possible sprain in my wrist. I'm seeing my own doctor Thursday.
Please keep that appointment and follow your doctor's advice. Do you have health insurance?
Yes, through my job. Now can I talk to the lawyer?

You're almost done, I promise. Here's exactly what happens next. I'm sending your information to the attorney as soon as we hang up. The attorney reviews new cases the same day, and you'll get a call back by four o'clock this afternoon. Is this number the best one for that call?
Four o'clock. Fine. Yes, this number.
Thank you. And so you know, there's no cost to you to have the attorney review your case. We work on a contingency fee, so there's no fee unless there's a recovery.
Okay. That's... okay. Sorry I was short with you. It's been a bad week.

No apology needed, Ms. Ramos. Let me read it back. You slipped on a clear liquid leaking from a freezer case at Valley Fresh Market on Rainbow Boulevard on November first, an employee named Kevin said it had been leaking all morning, the manager made a report, your daughter took photos, and you were treated at the emergency room for a hip contusion and a possible wrist sprain. Did I miss anything?
Then you'll hear from the attorney by four today. Please have the emergency room paperwork and your daughter's photos ready. Thank you for calling Harbor and Pine.

calls.title: Agitated Dog Bite (1P)
calls.about: A first-party caller, the person who was bitten, angry after the dog owner's insurance company called him. Listen for de-escalation, the animal control report, the dog owner's insurance, and the advice not to give a recorded statement.
listen_for: Letting an angry caller finish, then acknowledging
Animal control report and the dog owner's details
The 3P homeowner's insurer and the request for a recorded statement
Photos of the wounds and the treatment timeline
lines: Thank you for calling Harbor and Pine Injury Law. This is Amy, intake specialist. How can I help you?

Yeah, hi. I just got off the phone with some insurance lady who wants me to give a recorded statement about my neighbor's dog biting me, and I am furious. Their dog tore up my arm and now they're acting like it's my fault!
That sounds really upsetting, and I'm glad you called before giving any statement. I'm going to help you get this to an attorney. May I have your name?
Thank you, Mr. Holloway. And the best number to reach you?
Seven zero two, five five five, zero nine one seven.
Seven zero two, five five five, zero nine one seven. And your date of birth?
Thank you. Can you tell me when and where the bite happened?

October twenty eighth, in the evening. I was walking on the sidewalk in front of my neighbor's house on Palomino Lane. Their gate was open, and their German shepherd ran out and grabbed my forearm. I didn't do anything to it. I was just walking!
I understand. Do you know the owner's name and address?
Gary Whitman. Forty two eighteen Palomino Lane.
Has the dog bitten anyone before, that you know of?
It went after the mail carrier in the spring. Everybody on the street knows it.
Thank you. Did anyone report the bite to animal control or the police?
Animal control came out that night. The officer gave me a card with a report number. Hang on. A C, two four, dash, one one eight three.
A C two four, dash, one one eight three. Thank you. What treatment did you receive?
I went to the emergency room. Eleven stitches, a tetanus shot, antibiotics. They told me I might need a plastic surgeon for the scar. And I'm a mechanic, I can't use my right arm right now.
I'm sorry. Did you take photos of the wounds?
My wife took pictures that night and every day since.
That's very helpful, please keep taking them. Now, the insurance call. Do you know which company it was, and do you have a claim number?
Northfield Mutual. It's Gary's homeowner's insurance. The lady said claim number H O, five five two seven zero. She wants the recorded statement by Friday.

Thank you. I can't give legal advice, but the attorney will want to speak with you before you give any statement. If they call again, you can politely tell them you're speaking with an attorney and take their contact information.
Good. Because I was about to tell her a few things.
I completely understand, and it's best to let the attorney handle that conversation. Do you have your own health insurance, Mr. Holloway?

Thank you. Let me confirm what I have. On October twenty eighth, Gary Whitman's German shepherd ran out of an open gate at forty two eighteen Palomino Lane and bit your right forearm while you were on the sidewalk. Animal control report A C two four, dash, one one eight three. You had eleven stitches at the emergency room, and Northfield Mutual, the owner's homeowner's insurer, has asked you for a recorded statement under claim H O five five two seven zero. Is that all correct?
The attorney will call you today, before end of day, to talk about the statement and next steps. Is this number good for a call this afternoon?
Yes. Thank you. Sorry for yelling at the start.
You weren't yelling at me, Mr. Holloway. You've been through a lot. Please keep the animal control card, your hospital papers, and the photos together. Thank you for calling Harbor and Pine.

calls.title: Medical Malpractice: Worried About Attorney's Fees
calls.about: A caller whose husband's cancer was missed, who is afraid she can't afford a lawyer. Listen for how the VA explains the contingency fee without quoting a percentage, collects the medical timeline, and sets expectations about the expert review a malpractice case needs.
listen_for: Explaining a contingency fee in plain words, with no percentage promised
The treatment timeline: providers, dates, what was missed
Why a malpractice case needs an expert review first
Empathy without giving medical or legal opinions
lines: Thank you for calling Harbor and Pine Injury Law. This is Amy, intake specialist. How may I help you today?
Hi. I'm not even sure I should be calling. I don't think we can afford a lawyer.
I'm glad you called, and you're not committing to anything by talking with me. May I have your name?
Rosa Delgado. I'm calling about my husband, Tomas.
Thank you, Mrs. Delgado. What's the best number to reach you?
Seven two five, five five five, zero two zero four.

Seven two five, five five five, zero two zero four. Before we go further, let me answer your worry about cost, because I can hear it's on your mind. Our attorneys handle cases like this on a contingency fee. That means you pay no fee up front and no hourly bills. The attorney is paid a percentage of the recovery, only if there is one. If there's no recovery, you don't owe an attorney's fee.

The attorney explains the exact fee and the costs in writing at the consultation, before you sign anything, so I don't want to give you a number that isn't right for your case. And the consultation itself is free.
Can you tell me what happened to Tomas?

In January he went to his doctor, Dr. Harlan at Summit Family Clinic, with blood in his stool. The doctor said it was hemorrhoids and gave him a cream. He went back in April, still bleeding, and the doctor said the same thing. No tests.
I'm so sorry. What happened after that?
In August he collapsed at work. At the hospital they did a colonoscopy and found colon cancer. Stage three. The oncologist asked us why nobody had done a colonoscopy months ago.
Thank you for sharing that. May I have Tomas's date of birth?
Which hospital was he taken to in August, and what was the date?
Desert Springs Medical Center. August nineteenth.
Surgery in September, and he's in chemotherapy now. He can't work. He drove a delivery truck.

I understand. Is Tomas aware you're calling, and would he be able to join the consultation? Because he's the patient, the attorney will need to speak with him and get his authorization to request his records.
Yes, he asked me to call. He's sitting right here.

Thank you. One more thing I want you to know, so there are no surprises. Medical malpractice cases are reviewed differently from other injury cases. Before the firm can take one, the attorney usually has the medical records reviewed by a medical expert. So the attorney may not be able to tell you on the first call whether the firm can take the case. That's normal, and it isn't a no.
Okay. How long does that take?

The attorney will explain the timeline at the consultation. These cases also have strict deadlines, so it's good that you're calling now. Do you have any paperwork from the clinic visits or the hospital?
We have the discharge papers from August and the surgery records. Nothing from the clinic.

That's fine. The firm can request the clinic records with Tomas's authorization. Let me read back what I have. Tomas Delgado, born February eleventh, nineteen sixty eight, saw Dr. Harlan at Summit Family Clinic in January and April for rectal bleeding and was treated for hemorrhoids with no testing. On August nineteenth he collapsed and was diagnosed at Desert Springs Medical Center with stage three colon cancer, had surgery in September, and is in chemotherapy. Is that correct?
Can I schedule a free consultation with the attorney for you and Tomas this Thursday at two in the afternoon, by phone?

You'll get a confirmation text and an email with the intake packet, including the medical authorization for Tomas to sign. Please have the hospital and surgery paperwork nearby. Do you have any other questions for me?
No. I feel better than when I called. Thank you, Amy.
You're very welcome, Mrs. Delgado. Please give Tomas our best. We'll talk Thursday at two.

consult.title: Sample Guide: PI Consultation with Atty. Magdalena
consult.about: A personal injury consultation between Atty. Magdalena (A) and a new client (C) after a rear-end collision. The PI equivalent of the interview recordings: listen, read the A / C transcript, and compare your minutes with the sample minutes.
lines: Good morning. This is Attorney Magdalena. Am I speaking with Daniel Reyes?
Yes, good morning, Attorney. This is Daniel.

Thank you for making time, Daniel. Today is Monday, November third, and this is your initial consultation about your car accident. I'll ask you some questions, explain how a case like this works, and tell you what happens next. Is that alright?
Let's start with the accident. When and where did it happen?
October twentieth, around five thirty in the evening. I was stopped at the red light on Flamingo Road at Decatur Boulevard, here in Las Vegas, and a pickup truck hit me from behind.
Were you fully stopped when you were hit?
Completely stopped. I'd been sitting at the light maybe ten seconds. I saw him in my mirror. He was looking down at his phone.
Did the police come to the scene?
Yes, Las Vegas Metro. The officer gave the other driver a ticket for following too closely. I have the event number on a slip of paper. L V two four, one zero two zero, zero three three one.
Good. We'll order the full report. Did you get the other driver's information?
His name is Brian Tate. His insurance is Silverline Auto. I took a picture of his insurance card.
I have Granite State Insurance. I called them the next day to report it.
Did you give a recorded statement to Silverline, the other driver's insurance?
They called me twice. I didn't give a statement. I told them I'd talk to a lawyer first.
That was the right call. From today, if they call, you refer them to our office. Now, tell me about your injuries.
My neck and my upper back. The next morning I couldn't turn my head. I also had headaches for about a week, and my left shoulder has been tingling down to my fingers.

I went to urgent care the morning after, on October twenty first. They took X-rays and said nothing was broken, gave me muscle relaxers, and told me to see a chiropractor. I started chiropractic at Spine and Motion Clinic on October twenty fourth. I go three times a week.
And the tingling in your arm, has anyone looked at that?
The chiropractor wants me to get an MRI. I haven't scheduled it because I wasn't sure who pays for it.

That's a common worry. We'll help you with that. Please don't let cost stop you from getting the care your doctors recommend. Gaps in treatment can hurt both your recovery and your case. Has your work been affected?
Yes. I'm a warehouse supervisor. I missed six days, and I'm on light duty now, so I'm losing overtime.
Do you have pay stubs from before the accident?
Good. Have you ever injured your neck or back before?
No, never. Not even a sprain.
The rear bumper and the trunk were crushed. Silverline wrote an estimate of four thousand two hundred dollars, and the car is at Desert Auto Body now.

Alright. Let me explain how this works. You have a claim against Brian Tate, through his insurance, Silverline. A rear-end collision where the other driver was cited is generally strong on liability, but we still prove it with the police report and your photos. Your damages include your medical bills, your lost wages, the damage to your car, and your pain and suffering. In Nevada you generally have two years from the date of the accident to file a lawsuit, so there's time, but we start building the claim now.
Okay. How much does this cost me?

We work on a contingency fee. You pay nothing up front. Our fee is a percentage of the recovery, and it's written in the retainer agreement you'll read before you sign. If there's no recovery, you don't owe us a fee.
And how long does a case like this take?

Most of the time is your treatment. We wait until you've finished treating, or your doctor says you've improved as much as you will, so we know the full value of your claim. Then we send a demand to the insurance company and negotiate. I won't promise a timeline, but my team will update you regularly, and you can call us anytime.

Here are the next steps. First, my team will email you the retainer agreement and our intake packet today, including the medical authorization. Please sign and return them by Wednesday. Second, we'll send letters of representation to Silverline and to Granite State, so all calls go through us. Third, please schedule the MRI this week, and keep going to chiropractic. Fourth, send us the photos of the accident, the insurance card picture, your pay stubs, and the urgent care papers.
Got it. Anything I shouldn't do?
Yes. Don't post about the accident or your injuries on social media, and don't sign anything from an insurance company. If anyone calls you about the accident, give them our number.
Thank you, Daniel. My assistant will follow up with you on Wednesday to confirm we've received everything. Take care of yourself.

minutes.purpose: Initial consultation on Daniel Reyes's rear-end motor vehicle collision of October 20 (PI case evaluation and onboarding)
minutes.concerns:
Who pays for the MRI the chiropractor recommended (not yet scheduled because of cost).
How much the case will cost him.
How long a case like this takes.
What he should not do while the case is open.
minutes.advice:
Do not let cost stop recommended care; gaps in treatment hurt recovery and the case.
Contingency fee: nothing up front; the fee is a percentage of the recovery, set out in the retainer agreement; no fee if no recovery.
The case is valued after treatment ends (or maximum improvement), then a demand is sent and negotiated; no timeline promised.
Nevada generally allows two years from the accident to file a lawsuit.
Refer all insurance calls to the firm; do not give recorded statements, sign insurer documents, or post about the accident or injuries on social media.

Firm: email the retainer agreement and intake packet (with the medical authorization) today.
Client: sign and return the retainer and packet by Wednesday.
Firm: send LORs to Silverline Auto (3P) and Granite State Insurance (1P).
Firm: order the LVMPD report, event no. LV24-1020-0331.
Client: schedule the MRI this week; continue chiropractic 3x a week at Spine and Motion Clinic.
Client: send accident photos, the photo of the 3P insurance card, pre-accident pay stubs and the urgent care records.
Assistant: follow up with the client on Wednesday to confirm everything is received.
discussion: Atty. Magdalena opened the initial consultation and explained its agenda: the client's account, how the case works, and next steps.

Accident: October 20, about 5:30 PM. The client was fully stopped at a red light on Flamingo Rd at Decatur Blvd, Las Vegas, and was rear-ended by a pickup truck; he saw the other driver looking at his phone.
Police: LVMPD responded and cited the other driver for following too closely. Event no. LV24-1020-0331.

Parties and insurance: the at-fault driver is Brian Tate, insured by Silverline Auto (3P; the client photographed the insurance card). The client's own carrier is Granite State Insurance (1P), notified the next day.
Silverline called twice for a recorded statement; the client declined and gave none. The attorney confirmed this and said to refer all calls to the firm.
Injuries: neck and upper back pain, headaches for about a week, and tingling from the left shoulder to the fingers.

Treatment: urgent care on October 21 (X-rays negative, muscle relaxers, referred to a chiropractor); chiropractic at Spine and Motion Clinic from October 24, three times a week. The chiropractor recommended an MRI, not yet scheduled because of cost.
Lost wages: warehouse supervisor; missed six days and now on light duty, losing overtime. Pay stubs available.
No prior neck or back injuries.
Property damage: rear bumper and trunk; Silverline estimate $4,200; vehicle at Desert Auto Body.

The attorney explained liability (rear-end with a citation, proved by the police report and photos), the damages (medical bills, lost wages, property damage, pain and suffering), and Nevada's general two-year filing deadline.
Fees: contingency fee, nothing up front; the percentage is set in the retainer agreement; no fee without a recovery.
Timeline: the claim is valued after treatment ends, then a demand is sent and negotiated; no timeline promised; regular updates.
Next steps and instructions agreed (see action items); no social media posts, no signing insurer documents.
